circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island spans 5. 281 kilometers and was designed by Hermann Tilke to host the Formula One season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern venue for Formula One, following Bahrain and preceding tracks in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various support categories. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence and serves as a premier motorsport destination in Australia.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a storied history hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct eras, first as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then after reconstruction and renaming as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003. The track underwent significant modifications between these periods, including a shortening of its original layout.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street circuit in Azerbaijan's capital city, positioned along Baku Boulevard with a lap length of 6. 003 km, making it the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The venue first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016, before establishing itself as the home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Bahrain International Circuit opened in 2004 as a 5. 412 km facility hosting numerous motorsport categories. It was notable for staging the first Formula One championship race in the Middle East that same year, and continues to accommodate the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other series and endurance events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport venue features a balanced layout of extended straights and diverse corner complexities that test multiple racing disciplines. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located near the Belgian town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit in the Walloon region has been a staple of international motorsport since 1925. The venue hosted one of the inaugural Formula One races in 1950 and has regularly featured on the championship calendar since 1985, serving as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix with only two absences in the modern era.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometers and serves as Canada's premier Formula One venue, hosting the Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond top-tier single-seaters, the track has accommodated various international motorsport competitions including sportscar and open-wheel racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Jiading, has been the primary venue for China's Formula One grand prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. Beyond hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, the facility expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: The Silverstone Circuit near Northamptonshire in England has been the traditional venue for Britain's Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. Though the British Grand Prix alternated between three tracks from 1955 to 1986, it became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the circuit also regularly stages motorcycle racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted Formula One's first Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when racing commenced there in 1986. Originally envisioned as a street layout in Budapest's main park following Monaco's model, the government instead constructed the facility outside the city adjacent to a major highway, completing it in just eight months, faster than any contemporary Formula One venue.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit established in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, missing only 1980 for renovations, making it one of Formula One's most historic and consistent venues, earning its nickname "Temple of Speed" for its emphasis on high-speed straights and corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is renowned for hosting Formula One races alongside the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course navigating through Paradise, Nevada, that follows sections of the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its concentration of major hotels and casinos. The layout incorporates several iconic Las Vegas landmarks, including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban streets.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents decades apart. The track has returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 following a 23-year absence, now using an updated configuration distinct from the layout used during its previous hosting periods through 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners where Formula One cars achieve qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects for the Miami Grand Prix's debut on the F1 calendar in 2022, the track now hosts both single-seater racing and, from 2025–26, an adapted configuration for electric racing.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbour of the principality. Though officially named for Monaco itself, the track is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of its layout traverses that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track renowned for its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners that wind through the coastal landscape. The venue hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026, earning its nickname "The Roller coaster in the Dunes" for the exhilarating combination of rapid height variations and corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz that challenge drivers with their unique banking.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated near Lusail north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash eight years earlier. The track runs counterclockwise and features an associated kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront. Since 2021, it has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, establishing itself as a key fixture on the world championship calendar.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the urban areas of Downtown Core and Kallang into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, the 4. 657 km Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One teams. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and provides seating for approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major motorsport events including MotoGP and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race. The track has previously served as a venue for various racing series spanning from sports cars to rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish racing driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 Grand Prix victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship, making him the only driver to win both Formula One's and World Endurance's top championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed nine race victories following his entry into the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team, bringing his extensive motorsport background to the sport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish competitor, currently drives for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his racing tenure.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri stands as a notable achievement in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding the joint-record of seven world championships alongside Michael Schumacher. The driver has accumulated the most race victories (106), pole positions (105), and podium finishes (208) in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing significant endurance racing credentials after claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor who drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque driver currently racing for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in endurance racing for BMW through WRT, while also taking part-time NASCAR commitments with Trackhouse Racing. He previously raced in Formula One across two separate stints, competing in the series from 2014-2020 before returning for the 2022-2024 seasons.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Great Britain in Formula One, driving for McLaren where he secured the World Drivers' Championship in 2025. The British pilot has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The accomplished driver previously claimed victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from over 15 seasons in the sport. The veteran competitor finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the championship.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo, known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career before retiring from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition for Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve role with both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After five seasons as a full-time competitor starting in 2021, he transitioned to a backup position for the 2026 campaign.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen, a driver with Dutch and Belgian heritage, has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing. His career achievements include 73 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 12 seasons of competition in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One, having previously competed in the championship from 2022 through 2024. He holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese competitor to have participated in Formula One racing.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based squad has competed as Alpine since 2021, serving as Renault's factory team under the Alpine sports car brand. Originally known as Renault F1 Team and backed by Groupe Renault and its automotive alliance partners, the team maintained this works status until Renault's departure from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with its current racing operation competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian manufacturer Ferrari, stands as the most decorated and longest-running team in Formula One history, participating continuously since the championship's inaugural 1950 season. Renowned by the nickname "the Prancing Horse," the team has established itself as the sport's most successful competitor over its seven-decade tenure.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed F1 team in 2014, with operations beginning in the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu has served as team principal since January 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who held the position throughout the team's first eight years of competition.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber was a Swiss racing engineering firm established in 1970 that competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards as an independent constructor. The team achieved significant success in endurance racing, including victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours, before departing the sport in 2025 as one of the longest-serving constructors in the championship's history. Audi acquired the operation in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its own Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking, competing under the McLaren Mastercard F1 Team designation. The team operates as part of the broader McLaren Group structure, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through team ownership and engine supply. The current team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz, Ineos, and Toto Wolff from January 2022. Historically known as the "Silver Arrows," Mercedes teams have established themselves as a significant force in the sport.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team established in 2024, serving as Red Bull's second constructor alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a presence near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as part of the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competition in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with additional facilities near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the outfit represents Red Bull GmbH's dual-team strategy in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has become one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams in the sport. The outfit was under Christian Horner's management for two decades until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role thereafter.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. The team, currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters on a substantial 60-acre facility.
